title: Computer systems fundamentals: OS, networks and databases
goal: Understand what happens beneath your code: processes and memory, the network stack, and how databases store and query data, so that design trade-offs later rest on real mechanisms.

steps.title: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces
steps.note: Free. Read virtualization (CPU and memory) and concurrency first.

steps.title: Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach (companion site)
steps.note: Follow the application, transport and network layers; use the free lecture videos.

steps.title: CMU 15-445 Database Systems
steps.note: Lecture videos and notes on storage, indexing, query execution and transactions.

steps.title: Glossary
steps.note: Look up any term that is new; follow its related links.

steps.title: Build a tiny database
steps.brief: Implement a key-value store with a write-ahead log, a simple index and crash recovery, then add a text protocol over TCP. Measure throughput before and after adding the index.
steps.deliverable: A repository with the store, a test that kills the process mid-write and recovers, and a benchmark table in the README.

exit: You can explain what a page fault, a context switch and a TCP handshake are and when each hurts performance.
You can read an EXPLAIN plan and say why an index is or is not used.
Your tiny database survives a kill -9 during writes without losing acknowledged data.
